provenance: Ground truth labelled by hand on 2026-09-05 from two detector failures David reported the same day, and extended on 2026-09-07 with the Amazon Prime span the review named as an evaluation gap, per-case `provenance`, and a top-level `gaps` inventory of reviewed incidents that have no case because their input or labels no longer exist. Extended again on 2026-09-08 with a Practical AI episode David reported the same day, whose two surviving host reads are the first labelled soft-open reads in the corpus and the first labelled cues that straddle an advertising boundary. Timings are read from the aligned-STT cache entry the detector itself consumed, so a replay sees byte-identical input. No podcast prose or audio is stored here: each case points at a cache entry by sourceHash and the harness resolves it locally at run time. `audioDurationSeconds` is what the detector's own `probe_duration` saw: preparation overwrites the download in place, so it is derived as the cut file's measured duration plus the spans the run removed, rather than probed from an original that no longer exists.

closedBy.verdict: pass -- every labelled span is where it should be; keepLossSeconds 0.0, unknownCutSeconds 0.0, labelledCoverage 0.9476
closedBy.before: The detector cut 6.72-187.48 as one span, taking all 8.48s of the labelled must-keep at 179.00-187.48 plus the 11.68s of unlabelled cue-9 tail. The delivered file opened mid-sentence, several words into the host's first line.
closedBy.after: The detector cuts 6.72-167.32. The must-cut block is still 100% removed and no programme is touched.
closedBy.change: A new worker safeguard, trim_straddling_span_tails in Producer/Workers/wilted_pipeline.py, asks _program_starts_inside about the cue a span ends on and stops at that cue's start when the programme resumes inside it. The archive detector is unchanged: it produced 6.72-187.48 before and after, and every other worker recovery stage left that span alone, so the safeguard is the whole of the fix. It reuses the probe the oversized-span resize has always used for this question; what was missing was asking it on a span that no size bound ever flagged, because 180.76s of 390.27s is 46.3% and the single-span ceiling is 50%.
closedBy.failDirection: Only an affirmative answer trims, which is the opposite of the resize path's rule and deliberately so. That caller has already been told the programme resumes nearby and is only choosing how far to stop short, so it reads an unreadable answer as a yes. This safeguard screens every span in the episode with no such warrant, and trimming on silence would let one bad model response shave the tail off every correct cut in the file -- a defect the listener meets every episode, traded against one they meet rarely. First written the other way, which broke 22 of the worker suite's 371 tests: in each the probe was unanswerable and every span lost its final cue. On this case the model answers an explicit true, so the trim rests on a verdict rather than on a fallback.
closedBy.coverage: Scored on 1 of the 4 manifest cases. The other three -- waveform-two-preroll-sponsor-reads, pchh-preroll-swallowed-the-premise and practical-ai-two-host-reads-left-whole -- are unrunnable: their aligned-STT inputs were evicted from the 32-entry preparation cache before the pinned store existed (see decision corpus-inputs-are-pinned-not-cached), and on 2026-09-18 a search of the pinned store, the preparation cache, the repository and both temp roots found none of the three sourceHashes anywhere on disk. This matters more than usual here, because two of the three are themselves preroll over-cut cases and so are the nearest thing to a regression test for this edge. Until an input for one of them is recovered or relabelled from a fresh capture, this fix is validated on one episode.
closedBy.reproduce: ~/.venvs/wilted/bin/python Producer/Workers/ad_corpus.py --mode replay --json  (non-strict, because --strict fails the three unrunnable cases rather than skipping them; under --strict the corpus cannot pass at all while their inputs are missing)
closedBy.unitTests: StraddlingSpanTailTests in Producer/Workers/test_wilted_pipeline.py -- six cases covering the straddle, the advertising-throughout tail that must be left alone, the unanswerable probe that must change nothing, a span already refined off a cue edge, a span confined to one cue, and the probe budget. Mutation-checked: forcing the trim unconditionally fails three of them. The full worker suite is 377 tests green, up from 371; the one pre-existing test that changed is the superhuman-boundary call-sequence assertion, which now names the third model call this safeguard adds.
closedBy.twoPassRefusal: Already satisfied before this change, and re-checked rather than assumed. A span neither review will vouch for does not fall through to a zero exit: analyze_ad_detections compares the anchors covered by the proposed spans against those covered by the surviving ones and raises WorkerError('ads-recovery-audit-failed') -- 'explicit sponsor anchors were dropped after review twice declined to vouch for the span covering them' -- at Producer/Workers/wilted_pipeline.py:4159, after emitting ads.detect.recovery.audit.failed. Covered by test_post_cut_audit_fails_if_a_proposed_explicit_anchor_is_dropped in Producer/Workers/test_wilted_pipeline.py, which asserts the code rather than only the raise.

decisions.question: Is an unpaid promotion for a sister show on the same network advertising?
decisions.decision: No. An unpaid house promotion is not advertising. The detector is not wrong to leave one in.
decisions.applies: Label such a span `acceptable-cut`, not `must-cut` and not `must-keep`. The decision settles what it is, not whether David minds losing it, so a replay still scores it neither way.
decisions.context: A sister-show pitch split at a cue boundary: the call to action fell outside the sparse run that nominated it.

decisions.question: Where does a corpus case's aligned transcript live?
decisions.decision: In the pinned input store under ~/Library/Application Support/Wilted/adcorpus-inputs/, keyed by sourceHash, not only in the preparation cache.
decisions.applies: A replay reads the pinned store first and falls back to the aligned-STT cache only when the pinned copy is absent; `ad-corpus-adopt SOURCE=<cache snapshot>` copies every manifest-named entry into ~/Library/Application Support/Wilted/adcorpus-inputs/ and reports each case it cannot satisfy. The store lives outside the repository because these are third-party copyrighted transcripts.
decisions.context: The preparation cache is a 32-entry least-recently-used working set, not a corpus store. All three original cases' inputs -- sha256:38166909883bb20ba662299aa4a63df7590e8eea5960b2616b46dfaab40f08b5, sha256:6089921a9f668de9a384cd71450f7e70ee279d600cfcd82d42d686874ec4d469, and sha256:6664deea61754c68ceef94bb66b22fee6cc212c9629dbe19966ed95241517d2a -- were evicted before the 2026-09-17 replay, which returned 0/3 with 'no cached transcript'.
